name: Caraway
flavorNotes: and peppery with a hint of citrus
summary: An anise-adjacent seed with a warm, slightly bitter, licorice-tinged flavour. Essential in North African chile pastes and Central European baking.
description: Caraway seeds resemble cumin but taste quite different — they carry a warm anise character without being as intensely liquorice as fennel. They are the defining flavour of harissa and many North African spice pastes, as well as rye breads, sauerkraut, and Central European dishes. Toast lightly before using to bring out their volatile oils. Caraway bridges savoury spice cooking and baking like few other seeds.
culinaryUse: Caraway seeds are commonly used in a variety of cuisines, particularly in Central and Eastern European dishes, where they add a distinctive anise-like flavor to breads, sauerkraut, and meats. In German cuisine, they are essential in rye bread and sausages, imparting warmth and complexity. In North African cooking, caraway is an integral spice in chermoula and harissa, contributing depth to marinades and stews. Additionally, caraway pairs well with root vegetables, cheese dishes, and pickled foods, enhancing both savory and sweet profiles.
